BUF.body: Even though Buffalo has home-ice advantage, Tampa Bay has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Sabres’ best way through is getting good looks.

story.head: Dahlin’s favorite opponent
paras: The Sabres (8-5-3) beat Columbus 5-2 on Friday, and the Lightning have won two in a row. This is an Atlantic Division matchup, with the Lightning third (tied for seventh in the NHL) and the Sabres sixth (tied for 14th). The Atlantic has been the strongest of the four divisions so far.

The Lightning’s record (.733) is about what their chances are worth. The Sabres’ record (.594) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.540), largely thanks to pulling off wins in one-goal games.

The Lightning keep shots away better than almost anyone (3rd), get into a lot of chippy games (4th) and have had some of the best goaltending in the league (5th). The Sabres rarely get pinned in their own end (3rd) and get their shots through to the net (4th), but don't block many shots (30th). The Lightning have the edge over the Sabres on the penalty kill. Beyond that, the Bolts could find some good looks against the Sabres, who give up plenty of them.

Nikita Kucherov (4 G / 16 A / 20 P in 15 GP) leads the Lightning in scoring, with seven points in his last five games. Brandon Hagel (8 G / 9 A / 17 P in 15 GP) has a team-high eight goals. For the Sabres, Tage Thompson (10 G / 9 A / 19 P in 16 GP) leads the way in scoring, with ten points in his last five games. Jack Quinn (9 G / 7 A / 16 P in 16 GP) is next in line.

Andrei Vasilevskiy (8-3-1 / .886 SV% in 12 GS) will likely start for Tampa Bay, and Colten Ellis (3-2-0 / .891 SV% in 6 GS) for Buffalo. Vasilevskiy has a .855 save percentage in six starts against the Sabres, well under his usual .911. Don’t read much into it: a goalie’s record against one team rarely holds up.
